# G2 — inverse 5/3 IWT line core `iiwt_53_core` (2026-10-20)

**Level of evidence:** simulation (Icarus) + **post-synthesis** (Vivado 2026.1). No place-and-route,
no board.

## What changed

The core (hub `a8523aa`) was checked by one hand-written 8-sample line. It is now checked against the
**12 frozen IWT line vectors** (`tools/tag_reference/vectors/iwt_line_{len,s,d,in}.mem`, generated by
`gen_iwt_vectors.py` from `iwt_lifting.iwt1d_53`): feed `s` then `d`, require every original sample
back, at the right index, exactly once. Lines include length 2, ramps, impulses, ±32767/−32768,
alternating extremes, floor-sensitive negative sums and a random 512-sample line.

```
vivado/scripts/run_sim.sh iiwt_53_core
iiwt_53_core_tb: PASS (12 lines, perfect reconstruction of every iwt1d_53 vector)
```

The old `tb_iiwt_53.v` (one vector) is removed; `iiwt_53_core_tb.v` replaces it.

## Area fix

The first synthesis gave **7446 LUT (42.31 %) / 13425 FF (38.14 %) / 0 BRAM**, WNS +0.680 ns: the three
line buffers became flip-flops because they were written inside the reset block and `dbuf`/`ebuf`
were read at two addresses per cycle. Rewritten with the memories in a reset-free block, one read
port each, the neighbour sample (`d[k-1]` while computing, `even[k]` while emitting) held in a
register. Interface unchanged; output timing changed (the tb is timing-independent).

| | Slice LUTs | Slice Regs | BRAM | DSP | WNS @100 MHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| buffers as flip-flops (first) | 7446 | 13425 | 0 | 0 | +0.680 ns |
| **buffers as RAM (current)** | **220 (1.25 %)** | **112 (0.32 %)** | **1.5 tiles (3 × RAMB18)** | **0** | **+0.721 ns — met** |

Script: `results/hw_core_synth_2026-10-20_iiwt/core_synth.tcl`. Throughput ~2·len cycles per line
(load `len`, compute `len/2`, emit `len`). WNS margin is small (0.72 ns); a place-and-route run may need
the compute subtract registered.

## Mutation tests (current RTL)

| Mutation | FAIL lines |
|---|---|
| predictor rounding `+2` → `+0` | 295 |
| predictor `>>> 2` → `/ 4` (truncating division) | 200 |
| dropped `d[-1] = d[0]` replication | 9 |
| dropped `even[K] = even[K-1]` edge | 13 |
| update `>>> 1` → `/ 2` | 13 |

Two substitutions are **provable equivalences**, documented rather than claimed as caught (on the
first version of the RTL): predictor `>>>`→`>>` (the unsized literal `2` widens the sum to 32 bits, so
the difference is 3·2^30 ≡ 0 mod 2^18) and update `>>>`→`>>` (the result is truncated to 16 bits, and
the 18-bit sum of two 16-bit samples never needs bit 17).

## Still open

- Only 1D lines. A 2D inverse (rows + columns), composed as the forward tb does, is not tested.
- No place-and-route.
